subject: Request: Solstice multi-year term commitment — pricing & renewal protections
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@solstice.ai>, Courtney Lin <courtney.lin@solstice.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Solstice - draft 3yr proposal + redlines (for internal run)

Alex / Courtney — thanks again for the productive demo last week. Attached is a concise pricing summary and the draft commercial terms we discussed. Highlights: 3-year reserved commitment, up-front credit in year 1, and a proposed uplift cap to limit year-over-year increases.

Quick ask from your side: can you confirm the expected average monthly tokens and the primary region (US or EU) so we can right-size the Dedicated pool? We used your estimate of ~750M tokens/month in the attached deck.

We're going to route this through Deal Desk for an exception on the 3-year price lock and the renewal protection clause (see attached legal redlines). Karthik / Marissa — looping you for clearance to proceed with the specific concession set spelled out below if Solstice signs LOI by 12/10.

Proposed commercial ask (summary):
- Term: 36 months (start on activation)
- Year 1 effective unit discount: 18% off list for committed volume
- Uplift cap: max +5% year-over-year on unit price (post-year1)
- Renewal protection: automatic renewal at capped uplift; Solstice can request price re-open with 90 days' notice but cannot trigger earlier repricing during term
- Service level: 99.9% uptime target; service credits defined in SOW

Attachments: Solstice_Pricing_Summary_3yr.pdf, Deal_Deck_Solstice.pptx, Legal_Redlines_Solstice.docx

I will follow up with a short internal note outlining strategic rationale (logo, referenceable use-case, expected ARR) — happy to summarize live if you prefer.

-Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@solstice.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Courtney Lin <courtney.lin@solstice.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice - draft 3yr proposal + redlines (for internal run)

Thanks Neha — the deck looks good and aligns with what we discussed. Confirming:
- Average monthly tokens: 740-780M (US primary, small EU failover)
- We need the 36-month price lock to be explicit in the contract (no mid-term indexation except the stated uplift cap).

Two notes from our side:
1) We will ask legal to take a look at your redlines; expect comments on the renewal language and the data residency clause.
2) Can you option in a mid-term capacity increase addendum (we may need a +20% burst in year 2)? We'd prefer the price lock to apply to the committed baseline only; bursts billed at on-demand rates.

If you get internal clearance, please send signed LOI template and we'll get legal involved.

—Alex
Head of Platform, Solstice Analytics
alex.morales@solstice.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@solstice.ai>, Courtney Lin <courtney.lin@solstice.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Solstice - draft 3yr proposal + redlines — request for exec clearance (DL-89321)

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding the customer confirmation. Fast context: Solstice is high-growth analytics vendor (Series C) and a strategic logo for financial services use-cases. They want a 36-month commitment with a strict price lock and an uplift cap. They asked for an option to burst +20% capacity at on-demand rates.

Why this merits exception:
- Reference value: strong use-case for our observability customers and potential to expand to dedicated offering in Q3
- Committed ARR: estimated $6.1M TCV on the committed baseline (per attached pricing summary)
- Competitive: other vendors require step-ups; their procurement is pushing for multi-year predictability

Concession request (what I'm asking Deal Desk to approve):
- Approve 36-month firm price lock on committed baseline (no indexation except stated uplift cap)
- Approve Year 1 upfront discount 18% (to be modeled against expected volume)
- Approve uplift cap of +5% YoY max on unit price after Year 1
- Allow a burst addendum for +20% capacity at on-demand rates, not covered by the lock
- Renewal protection clause: auto-renew at capped uplift; Solstice can request re-open 90 days before renewal but re-pricing only upon mutual agreement or material usage change (>30% delta)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: long-term price exposure if costs rise (mitigate with uplift cap and ability to move them to new model variants)
- Risk: capacity over-commit (mitigate with burst cap and conservative capacity buffer in the SOW)

Attachments included for review: Solstice_Pricing_Summary_3yr.pdf, Legal_Redlines_Solstice.docx, Deal_Deck_Solstice.pptx

Requested action: please reply with Approve / Approve w/ legal tweak / Decline. If approve, can we sign off by EOD 12/03 so I can send LOI to the customer and start legal review?

Thanks — Neha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@solstice.ai>, Courtney Lin <courtney.lin@solstice.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Solstice - draft 3yr proposal + redlines — request for exec clearance (DL-89321)

Neha — thanks for the clear summary and rationale. Approve in principle with one legal condition.

Decision: APPROVED (commercial terms)
- 36-month price lock on committed baseline (approved)
- Year 1 discount: 18% (approved)
- Uplift cap: +5% YoY (approved)
- Burst addendum: allow +20% at on-demand rates (approved)
- Renewal protection: auto-renew with capped uplift; customer can request re-open at 90 days (approved)

Legal condition (required before LOI execution): Redwood legal must receive an explicit carve for service credits and a maximum aggregate liability cap that matches our standard enterprise playbook. I have asked Legal to prioritize and will include a one-paragraph amendment to the redlines.

Next steps:
1) Neha — send LOI with the approved commercial bullets and mark it "subject to legal final review."
2) Marissa — please create a Deal Desk record and checklist for on-boarding (billing, SSO, provisioning runbook).
3) Jordan / Legal — please coordinate the liability and service-credit carve and turn around the redlines by COB 12/07.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
